title: Prune unused results and streamline two extraction bounds

add.label: Ledger interpolation
add.name: Convex bound for the security ledger
add.statement: Under admissibility condition (P5), for every integer $0\le Q<2^\lambda$, $E(2Q+2)\le (Q+1)/2^\lambda$.
add.explain: Interpolate between the two endpoint bounds in (P5).
add.proof:
The quadratic polynomial $F(Q):=E(2Q+2)-(Q+1)/2^\lambda$ has coefficient $2\theta+20\varepsilon_f$ at $Q^2$ by the formula for $E$.
The nonnegative quadratic coefficient makes $F$ convex.
The first inequality in (P5) gives $F(0)\le 0$.
Adding the two inequalities of (P5) gives $F(2^\lambda-1)=E(2^{\lambda+1})-1\le 0$.
Convexity gives $F(Q)\le 0$ throughout $[0,2^\lambda-1]$.

add.label: Initial collision bound
add.name: Union bound for the initial mark
add.statement: A run has first mark $\mathsf{init}$ with probability at most $\sum_{s\in\{1,2,T\}}\binom{L_s}{2}\varepsilon_f$.
add.proof:
By (M1), a first mark $\mathsf{init}$ requires equal labels for a formally unequal pair among the $L_s$ received elements of some group $s\in\{1,2,T\}$.
By injectivity of the group label map, every such pair then has equal exponents.
The union bound over the $\binom{L_s}{2}$ unordered received pairs in each group gives $\Pr[\text{first mark is }\mathsf{init}]\le\sum_{s\in\{1,2,T\}}\binom{L_s}{2}\varepsilon_f$.

edges.demand: For any formally unequal pair of received expressions in G_1 or G_2, the probability of equal exponents over the encryption coins is at most ε_f. The same bound holds for the sole received pair in G_T, whose exponent difference 1−ακ is nonidentically zero at every fixed r.

discharge.argument: The statement is the demanded bound with the same range and (P5) premise.
The statement is the demanded initial-mark probability bound.
